drills.label: Cold open
drills.question_line: SAM: A retail team's service writes product descriptions with Claude.
drills.answer_line: SAM: That is the constraint that rules batch out.
drills.stem: On each catalogue import, a service uses the async client to fire 5,000 requests at once. Descriptions must be ready within the hour. About half fail with 429. What is the best fix?

options.A: Cap requests in flight, sized to the rate limits, and let the SDK's retries honour retry-after
options.B: Wrap every call in a loop that retries immediately until it succeeds
options.C: Move the job to the Message Batches API
options.D: Switch to the largest model so each request does more

drills.why: "Within the hour" rules out batch, whose results can take up to 24 hours. Bursts drain the token bucket; cap concurrency and let retries honour retry-after.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. For each statement, say true or false.
drills.prompt: True or false: (1) retry a 400 invalid_request with backoff; (2) retry a 429 after its retry-after seconds; (3) retry a 529 overloaded with backoff; (4) a 401 usually clears after a few retries.
drills.answer: False, true, true, false. 400 and 401 fail the same way every time: fix the request or the key. 429 and 529 are transient: back off and retry.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. Choose two. A field service company's dispatch assistant
drills.answer_line: SAM: Both. A removes the dependency on wording
drills.stem: Choose two. A dispatch assistant uses a hand-written HTTP client. Its rate-limit handling broke when an error message's wording changed, and support asked for a failing request's identifier that was never stored. Which two changes fix these at the root?

options.A: Move to the official SDK and catch its typed rate limit exception instead of matching message text
options.B: Record the request ID from each failed response in the application logs
options.C: Add more phrases to the message-matching code to catch new wordings
options.D: Set the SDK's retries to zero and retry forever in application code
options.E: Switch to a larger model so fewer requests fail

drills.why: Typed exceptions follow the status, not the prose; the request ID is what support needs. C patches the symptom, D loses backoff, E is "bigger".

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. A healthcare provider's patient-portal assistant
drills.answer_line: SAM: B leaks the key outright
drills.stem: A patient-portal assistant in a single-page web app must show Claude's reply as it is written and let the patient press stop mid-answer. What is the best design?

options.A: Browser websocket to the backend; backend keeps the key, streams from the Messages API, relays events, closes on stop
options.B: Ship the API key in the front-end code so the browser calls the Messages API directly
options.C: Make a non-streaming call and have the browser poll every second
options.D: Open a websocket from the browser straight to the Messages API

drills.why: The Messages API streams over server-sent events; two-way websockets belong between browser and backend, and the key stays on the server.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. A bank must move four hundred services
drills.answer_line: SAM: B. It plans before editing
drills.stem: A bank must move 400 services from a deprecated internal logging client to its replacement. Behaviour must not change, and every change must be reviewable. What is the best approach?

options.A: One interactive session: "migrate every service", relying on checkpoints to undo mistakes
options.B: Plan mode, confirm test coverage, scripted claude -p loop with pre-approved tools on 2-3 services first, then the rest
options.C: Switch to the model with the largest context window so all 400 fit in one session
options.D: Have each owner paste code into a chat and apply suggestions by hand

drills.why: Plan, make behaviour checkable, pilot, then fan out in reviewable changes. Checkpoints miss shell commands and do not replace git; context size is "bigger".

drills.question_line: SAM: Recall first. Pause and name the four segments, and the giveaway for each.
drills.answer_line: ALEX: REST and JSON, where the giveaway is the status code.
drills.prompt: Name the four segments, and the giveaway for each.
drills.answer: REST and JSON: the status code. SDKs: a hand-written client. Async and streaming: a 429 burst or a key in the browser. Version control to refactoring: a committed secret or a one-shot migration.

What the official SDK does, so you stop rebuilding it
Server-sent events and websockets in a streaming app
Version control, CI, code review and refactoring with Claude Code
Cold open: the catalogue import: Two skills: 7.4% and 6.1%, about seven items
POST /v1/messages: API key, anthropic-version, content-type JSON
content is a list of typed blocks: text, tool_use, thinking
Check block type and stop_reason before parsing
Errors are JSON: type, message, request ID
The status code decides between fixing and retrying
Segment two: SDKs that wrap REST: SDK sets headers and types requests and responses
Retries connection, rate limit and server errors: 2 by default, backoff
Honours retry-after; Python default timeout 10 minutes
Streaming helpers assemble the final message
Don't stack your own retry loop on the SDK's: 3 x 3 = 9 calls
Segment three: async, streaming and webs: Async client: many calls in flight; no sync client in an async server
Rate limits: RPM, input and output tokens per minute, token bucket
Short bursts can exceed the limit; cost-first and tomorrow: batch
Messages API streams via server-sent events: one-way over HTTP
Websocket: persistent, two-way; errors can arrive after a 200
Tool input streams as partial JSON: parse at content_block_stop
Segment four: version control, CI, revie: Keys: env var, gitignored .env, CI repository secret
Checkpoints don't replace git; worktrees for parallel sessions
CI: claude -p with JSON output, or the Claude Code GitHub Action
Review in a fresh context: writer and reviewer
One-sentence diff: skip plan mode and run the tests
Cold open: the verdict: Answer: A, cap requests in flight and honour retry-after
"Within the hour" rules out batch: up to 24 hours
B hammers the limit and ignores retry-after
D changes nothing about the request rate
Tell: a deadline in minutes plus a 429 burst
Five to remember: REST and JSON: check block type and stop_reason before parsing
Invalid request, auth, permission: fix. 429, 529, 5xx: back off and retry
Official SDK: 2 retries, timeouts, typed exceptions, request ID
Async, capped to rate limits; SSE from the API, websockets client to backend
Commit config not keys; claude -p in CI; fresh reviewer; plan, test, pilot
Recap: the exam tells: Parses only sometimes → max_tokens stop or non-text first block
Invalid request or authentication → fix, don't retry
Matches error text or own retry loop → official SDK, typed exceptions
Support wants to trace a call → the request ID
All at once, half 429 → capped concurrency; overnight and cost → batch
Websocket to the Messages API → it streams over SSE
Key in a browser or workflow file → server side or secret store
Self-review → fresh reviewer; 400 services → plan, test, pilot, fan out
